clue.text: Live in old vessel in Cyprus

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is held inside it, so the vessel sits within the country's letters

parts.note: CY is the international vehicle code for Cyprus
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: Someone moving home to an antique boat moored in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyprus is shortened to its international vehicle code, which then holds the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a house is to dwell there as its resident.

clue.text: Rival's work attitude embraces an indefinable quality

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug something, so the attitude word wraps around the quality word

parts.note: a pose is an assumed attitude
'it' is that special something, as in an It girl

explanation.surface: A competitor's professional bearing hides some elusive charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: An indefinable quality is 'it', the star quality in the phrase 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Your opposite, or opposite number, is the person facing you in a contest, a counterpart or competitor.

clue.text: Finding faults serious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inclined to point out flaws
second meaning: grave, as of a patient's condition

explanation.surface: A grave discovery of defects.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both a carping, censorious attitude and a dangerous condition such as a hospital patient's.

clue.text: Teacher poses for shot with Queen

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An academic sits for a photograph alongside the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a photograph, but it signals the letters of 'poses for' plus R being mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor is a university teacher of the highest rank.

clue.text: About to return money? Editor's stressed

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the short word for about is read backwards

parts.note: CA, circa, means about
a cent is a coin, a unit of money
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is anxious about getting money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stressed' reads as anxious, but it means emphasised in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An accented syllable is one given emphasis when spoken, so it is stressed.

clue.text: Great mind — intelligent

parts.note: to mind something is to consider it, think about it
an able person is clever

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant, clever intellect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' looks like a noun here, but it is the verb meaning to heed or think about.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerable amount is a large or substantial one, so great in size.

clue.text: More irrelevant? Not half!

indicators.note: keeping no more than half means dropping the back five of the ten letters

parts.note: extraneous means irrelevant to the matter in hand

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is further beside the point, answered with an emphatic British 'not half!' meaning 'absolutely'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it literally removes half of EXTRANEOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, so it can stand for further or more of something.

clue.text: Catch up with leaders in nerve-wracking, if short, game

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to net something is to catch it

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Pulling level with the front-runners in a tense but brief match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' feels like it is trimming a word, but it is just the third word supplying its leader; 'up' turns the catch word over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a familiar example of a game.

clue.text: Seeing American lawyer can start to grind

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney in the US
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Meeting a US attorney who is able to begin some hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing someone, in the romantic sense, means going out with them regularly.

clue.text: Bird is in for nuts, primarily

indicators.note: the little verb is put in, so it sits inside the other letters

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: primarily points at the first letter of the word just before it

parts.note: opening letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small bird is eager for nuts above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a jail term, from rhyming slang 'bird lime' = time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird is slang for serving a jail sentence, so bird means prison.

clue.text: Charged this month in court

parts.note: INST, instant, is the old business-letter shorthand for this month
taken as written
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone was formally accused this month in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a criminal charge; it means filled or imbued, as in 'instinct with life'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, instinct with something means full of it or imbued with it, charged with energy.

clue.text: Girl's set to be let down

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and the apostrophe S joins it
a set time is an appointed time

explanation.surface: A young woman is about to be disappointed by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling let down means being saddened because hopes were not met.

clue.text: Rat's small and white, perhaps

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
white is one kind of wine, as the 'perhaps' signals

explanation.surface: A description of a laboratory rat that is little and pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' reads as the rodent's colour, but it is an example of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both insults name a contemptible, nasty person.

clue.text: Check abandoned line for cod

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so the letter for the line is dropped

parts.note: a limitation is a check or restraint
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A fishing line is given up when angling for cod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' looks like the fish, but as an adjective it means mock or fake, as in cod Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod, used before a noun, means sham or pretend, and an imitation is a fake copy.

clue.text: Frank rants about relative

indicators.note: turned about means moved around, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
a parent is a close relation

explanation.surface: A man called Frank grumbles about a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent dealings are open and honest, with nothing hidden, so frank.

clue.text: Long journey cut short by maiden with large jewellery — a sign of fear?

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a trek is a long, arduous journey
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
bling is showy, chunky jewellery

explanation.surface: A traveller on a long walk weighed down by an outsized necklace, looking nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that shaking is one example of a sign of fear among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking or quivering is an involuntary physical symptom of being frightened.

clue.text: Exquisite iced tea drunk around end of meal

indicators.note: around means placed on all sides, so the rearranged letters surround one more letter
drunk means unsteady and muddled, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cold tea drunk at the close of a fine dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as past participle of drink, as the tea would be, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate and exquisite both describe something finely made and refined in quality.

clue.text: Went to embrace nurse in awkward date

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the rearranged letters hug another word
in places the care word inside the shuffled letters
something awkward is clumsy and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to tend a patient is to nurse them

explanation.surface: On an uncomfortable evening out, someone moved in to hug a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To have attended an event is to have gone to it, been present.

clue.text: Let man creep off to get substitute

indicators.note: something off is wrong or gone bad, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager lets a sluggish player slip off so a sub can come on.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement is something or someone put in place of another, a stand-in.

clue.text: Brilliance one's shown in class

indicators.note: something shown in a place is displayed within it, so the numeral goes inside

parts.note: a genus is a class in biological classification
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pupil's brilliance shows during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' suggests a school lesson but is the taxonomic rank. GEN(I)US.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius is exceptional intellectual or creative power, a brilliance of mind.

clue.text: Learn if criminal female goes straight

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked and wrong, so these letters are rearranged
whatever goes leaves, so the female letter departs

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman offender is told she will find out if she goes straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes straight' sounds like reforming; really 'goes' removes F, and 'straight' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged in or moving along a straight line.

clue.text: I adore it terribly, Steel's latest newspaper article

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its final one

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gushing reader praises a columnist named Steel for their most recent piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is an opinion piece in a newspaper written on behalf of its editors.

clue.text: Blunt axes succeeded in many instances

indicators.note: to axe something is to cut it, so the letter that follows is removed

parts.note: to blunt an edge or impact is to soften it
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Dull axes have frequently done the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like plural tools, but it is the verb: cutting S from SOFTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, on many occasions.

clue.text: Apparatus for a horse left out — groom will need one

indicators.note: left out means omitted, so that letter is removed from the tack word

parts.note: a bridle is the headgear used to control a horse
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Stable talk: a horse's tack is missing and the stable groom must have it.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse imagery makes 'groom' a stable hand, but here it is a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom cannot marry without a partner, the woman he weds.

clue.text: I refuse to pen bird's name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to pen an animal is to enclose it, so the refusal word surrounds the bird

parts.note: to deny is to refuse
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone declines to write down the name of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing, but it means enclosing, as sheep are penned.
explanation.definitionFit: Your identity is who you are, the name by which you are known.

clue.text: Make fun of a learner? Daughter's mean

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
taken as written
L is the learner-driver plate
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Is teasing a learner driver unkind, a daughter wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests unkind; here it is the older sense of low or base.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald humour is coarse and vulgar, and mean in its old sense means low or common.

clue.text: Piece of music composed without a key?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the calm word goes around the rest

parts.note: serene means calm and composed
taken as written
D is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A tune written with no key signature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like writing music; it means calm. 'Without' means outside, not lacking: SEREN(A D)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song or instrumental work, traditionally performed for a lover at evening.

clue.text: Admitted a sin

parts.note: taken as written
greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A confession of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a point is to concede or accept it, which is to have agreed.
